title: Review of c27's ringswim repair (SIBRM): 3 of 3 mature ringed swimmers on fresh seed 11 re-close their ring after a 40% front cut and regrow, one swims 4.0 BL after repair; with the label-free kernel drive the 4x smaller cells die from a 40% cut (3/3) but 2 of 3 repair a 20% cut
summary: Ran c27's twinrepair.py (exact branched twin, 40% front cut at t=10000, wound keeps its substrate, 2000 steps) on fresh seed 11 with the claim's world, and a labkit run of the world on seed 11. All 3 picked cells (area 251-337) repair: ring closure >= 0.9 at +100-140, ring >= 1.5 in 100% of second-half frames, area back to its pre-cut value at +360 for 2 of 3 (the third ends at its twin's area, 222 px); cell 22's repaired cell travels 4.0 BL (twin 1.2) (tr/label_s11/twinrepair.png). Construction test, the same cut with the world's label-free kernel drive (mu 0.75, kd 0.08, the window where kernel cells swim and divide): the picked cells are 4x smaller (66-97 px) and all 3 die within 40-60 steps of a 40% cut, while their twins live 1380-1980 steps (tr/kernel_s11). With a 20% cut, 2 of 3 kernel cells re-close their ring at +60-80 and regain their area at +180-460, and one dies at +80 (tr/kernel20_s11). So repair replicates in the claimed world, and with the local drive it survives only smaller cuts: what the cut leaves must stay above a viable size.

verdicts.limitation: M is by construction here as in the parent claim (per-body rigid label drive), and only 1 of my 3 repaired cells travelled >= 3 BL after the cut, so the joint 'repairs and swims on' rests on few cells; the ring's re-formation is partly built in (curvature flow, chi drift up the wall indicator), which the author states. My labkit run put the damage at the last frame (200 of 200), so it shows no post-cut frames; the twin tests carry the repair evidence. One fresh seed; kernel-drive arms at one mu/kd point.
